## Fixed
- **False "not in the source" results for mods with test projects in their repository.** The source comparison read every C# file in a repository. Repositories with test or tool projects can contain stand-in classes with the same names as the mod's own classes, and these were mixed into the comparison. It now compares only against the project that builds the mod's DLL, the way the compiler does: the files in that project's folder, minus subfolders that are projects of their own and files removed with `<Compile Remove>`, plus files it includes from elsewhere in the repository. If no project builds the DLL, the whole repository is used and the details say so.

## Improved
- **Mods whose repository is very large can now be compared.** A repository that is mostly other files, such as thousands of icons, could be over the download limit. When a download passes 50 MB, the app now fetches only the C# and project files (up to 50, one GitHub request each) instead of the whole repository.
- **`Assembly.Load` is rated by what it loads.** Loading code from memory (`Assembly.Load(byte[])`) stays High. Looking up another assembly by name, usually another installed mod for compatibility, is now Medium ("looks up another assembly by name").
- **Fewer false alarms for links.** Links to the mod's own GitHub repository (the one on its Paradox Mods page) and to Paradox Mods are no longer reported as suspicious text. Other web addresses still are.
- When Paradox Mods has no version text for a mod, the app shows Paradox's version number instead of nothing.

After updating, every mod is compared once more, so these changes apply to mods that were already checked.

## Download and verify
Download `CS2ModVerifier-v0.1.8-win-x64.zip`, extract it, and run `CS2ModVerifier.exe`. To update, exit the running app from the tray menu and replace the old `CS2ModVerifier.exe` with the new one. Your settings and ignored findings are kept.

**Windows SmartScreen will most likely warn you**, because the exe is not code-signed. Check the download first, then choose "More info" and "Run anyway".

This release was built by GitHub Actions from the tagged commit. To check that your download is that build:

```
gh attestation verify CS2ModVerifier.exe --repo KDanielK/CS2ModVerifier
```

Or compare the SHA-256 hash (`Get-FileHash CS2ModVerifier.exe`, or `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt`) with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Please note
CS2 Mod Verifier is an aid, not a guarantee of safety. No findings does not mean a mod is safe, and a finding does not mean a mod is harmful. See the README for what each check does and does not show.
